title: Manager in-Basket 30-day Simulator Kit
content:
Purpose:
This kit is a lightweight, reproducible in-basket simulation for managers joining Redwood Inference. It's designed to: help hiring panels validate leadership pattern-matching, give candidates/hires a realistic first-30-day problem set, and create a shared evidence record for onboarding success criteria. Use in interview loops for manager hires or as a first-week diagnostic for promoted ICs transitioning to managers.

How to run the simulator (recommended flow):
1) Pre-work (2–4 days before run):
   - Send candidate a short context pack: org chart (relevant team), three recent incident summaries, product roadmap snapshot, and 2 sample Slack threads.
   - Give 90 minutes of asynchronous time to review materials and prepare a 10–12 minute response deck or structured note.
   - Ask candidate to upload their materials to the loop's shared folder.
2) Live session (1.5 hours):
   - 10m: brief intro + goals from panel lead.
   - 50m: candidate presents their 10–12 minute plan followed by a 10–15m Q&A.
   - 30m: panel-run behavioral probes + role-play crisis (see scenarios below).
3) Score and calibrate (30–40 minutes immediately after):
   - Panel fills rubric independently, then convenes for a 15–20m calibration huddle.

Simulation materials (included in pack):
- Org snapshot: Product Manager (PM), Engineering Lead, 3 ICs, SRE partner, Solutions Eng contact.
- Incident brief: 3-day outage summary (root: misrouted traffic due to a rollout, partial mitigation applied).
- Roadmap pull: upcoming Dedicated launch with capacity targets and SLA promises.
- Stake notes: two customer escalation emails (one enterprise, one PLG power-user).
- Slack threads: cross-functional disagreement about rollback vs. hotfix.

Core scenarios for role-play (pick 1–2):
- Outage Triage: The SRE asks for an immediate rollback; product wants limited rollback due to feature gating. Candidate must recommend a path and marshal stakeholders.
- Hiring Freeze: Headcount reduced mid-quarter; candidate must prioritize roles to keep roadmaps realistic.
- Postmortem Crafting: Compose the first-draft postmortem and decide what to share publicly and what to keep internal.

Interview rubric (scoring 1–5; 1=weak, 3=meets, 5=exemplary) — capture evidence in short bullet form:
- Decisiveness under ambiguity: Did they pick a clear path + justify tradeoffs?
- Stakeholder management: Clarity, empathy, escalation plan and expected outcomes.
- Operational judgement: Understanding of risk, rollback costs, and mitigations (metrics indicated).
- Prioritization & resourcing: Can they reallocate effort and set measurable milestones?
- Communication & documentation: Draft clarity, audience-aware messaging, follow-up cadence.
- Team development lens: Coaching moments, career leveling, performance concerns handled.

Pass/fail thresholds (recommended):
- Hire strongly: median >=4 on Decisiveness, Stakeholder mgmt, Operational judgement; no score <=2 on any critical dimension.
- Hire: median >=3 across core categories and strong evidence of growth plan.
- No hire: any critical dimension <=2 and little plan to remediate.

Scoring guidance & anchors (examples):
- Decisiveness 5: Picks a pragmatic path within 5 minutes of the role-play, outlines timeline, rollback criteria, and contingency plan with metrics (latency, error rate, SLA impact).
- Stakeholder mgmt 3: Recognizes PM and SRE positions, proposes meeting cadence and who to brief; leaves some ambiguity on customer comms.
- Operational judgement 2: Misses cascade risks (cache invalidation, downstream batch jobs) or underestimates blast radius.

Onboarding checklist (first 30 days for new manager hire):
Week 0 (Before first day):
- Confirm first-week 1:1 schedule with manager and skip-level.
- Provide role simulator pack and ask to complete a reflective 1-pager pre-start.
- Ensure engineering access, metrics dashboards, and incident playbooks accessible.
Week 1:
- Shadow triage rotation (2 shifts): observe incident cadence and postmortem culture.
- Run 3 x 1:1s with direct reports focused on goals + immediate blockers; capture top 3 priorities per report.
- Deliver a 30-day plan draft to manager + peer feedback session.
Week 2:
- Lead one small cross-functional sync (PM, SRE, Solutions Eng) to re-prioritize backlog items.
- Complete hiring calibration (review open reqs, scorecards) with People Ops.
- Identify a coaching plan for at least one direct report (30/60/90).
Week 3–4:
- Own a production ops checklist (deploy, rollback runbook) and execute a dry-run with SRE.
- Present a 60-day roadmap update to stakeholders; solicit alignment.
- Schedule skip-level introduction + feedback collection.

Success metrics to track (first 90 days):
- Team stability: 1:1 coverage rate, direct-report satisfaction (pulse survey) >= baseline.
- Operational: Mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to restore (MTTR) improvements or stable against baseline within SLA windows.
- Hiring & ramp: 60-day acceptance and 90-day productivity signals met for prioritized hires.
- Delivery: Percentage of commitments met vs. committed for the 60-day plan.

Evidence journal template (recommended fields):
- Date, scenario, summary (2–3 bullets), rubric scores (numbers), panel notes (short bullets), follow-ups assigned (owner + due date).

Common probes for panelists (behavioral prompts):
- Tell us about a time you decided to roll forward rather than roll back—what did you consider?
- How do you balance short-term customer escalation fixes with long-term technical debt reduction?
- Describe a coaching moment you led that moved an underperforming engineer into a sustainable trajectory.

Hiring plan appendix (quick checklist for manager hires):
- Define role success profile (top 3 outcomes for first 6 months).
- Build a 4-step interview loop: recruiter screen, hiring-manager simulation (this in-basket), peer interview (system design or org-specific), final leadership calibration.
- Create a shared evidence folder before interviews (candidate artifacts + rubric entries).

Operational notes / Pitfalls to avoid:
- Don’t overload the candidate with >4 discrete problems—focus on depth, not breadth.
- Avoid making the role-play purely hypothetical; ground it with customer and metric signals.
- Ensure panel diversity: include at least one peer, one cross-functional partner, and one people-ops representative.

Next steps for People Ops team running the kit:
- Ship a trimmed version of this pack to recruiting as a standard template (HR-1247).
- Run a 2-week pilot with 6 manager hires; collect rubric calibration notes and pulse panelist satisfaction.
- Iterate simulation scenarios based on real outages or postmortem learnings from the previous quarter.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is experimental — intended to reduce time-to-evidence in manager hiring and surface early onboarding risks. Please add calibration examples and anonymized candidate notes to the linked Confluence page (DOCS-320) after each run.
